identificationModule.briefTitle: SSRI Antidepressant Fluoxetine Improving Immunotherapy Efficacy in Advanced Hepatobiliary Malignancy Patients With Depression and Anxiety
identificationModule.officialTitle: SSRI Antidepressant Fluoxetine Improving Immunotherapy Efficacy in Advanced Hepatobiliary Malignancy Patients With Depression and Anxiety: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial

leadSponsor.name: First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
Advanced liver and gallbladder malignancies (including liver cancer, cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder cancer) are a type of disease that is difficult to treat, and most patients have a short survival period. In recent years, immunotherapy (such as PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors) has brought new hope to these patients, but still only a small number of patients can benefit.

Research has found that approximately 40% of patients with liver and gallbladder tumors have symptoms of depression and anxiety, which not only affect their quality of life but may also reduce the therapeutic effect by influencing immune function. Fluoxetine is a commonly used antidepressant. The latest research shows that in addition to improving mood, it may also enhance the anti-tumor effect of immunotherapy. This study aims to explore whether fluoxetine combined with immunotherapy can better control tumors than immunotherapy alone, prolong the survival period of patients, and at the same time improve the depressive and anxious symptoms and quality of life of patients.

armGroups.label: Experimental Group
armGroups.description: 1\. Standard treatment plan For patients with hepatocellular carcinoma, the first-line treatment regimen containing PD-1 inhibitors /PD-L1 inhibitors is adopted: 1) Toripalimab + bevacizumab 2) Tislelizumab 3) Nivolumab + ipilimumab For patients with cholangiocarcinoma, the combination of PD-1 inhibitors /PD-L1 inhibitors and gemcitabine + cisplatin/oxaliplatin (such as pembrolizumab +GEM -CDDP or durvalumab +GEM -CDDP) is adopted. 2. Fluoxetine: Maintain at 20mg per day, orally, until disease progression or intolerance. 3. The use of antiemetic, analgesic and other symptomatic treatment drugs is allowed, and all concurrent medication situations should be recorded.

armGroups.label: Control Group
armGroups.description:
1\. Standard treatment plan

For patients with hepatocellular carcinoma, the first-line treatment regimen containing PD-1 inhibitors /PD-L1 inhibitors is adopted:

1. Toripalimab + bevacizumab
2. Tislelizumab
3. Nivolumab + ipilimumab For patients with cholangiocarcinoma, the combination of PD-1 inhibitors /PD-L1 inhibitors and gemcitabine + cisplatin/oxaliplatin (such as pembrolizumab +GEM -CDDP or durvalumab +GEM -CDDP) is adopted.

2\. Placebo: Take 1 placebo tablet per day for maintenance, orally.

3\. The use of antiemetic, analgesic and other symptomatic treatment drugs is allowed, and all concurrent medication situations should be recorded.

primaryOutcomes.description: Proportion of participants achieving complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) based on mRECIST criteria, measured on contrast-enhanced CT/MRI at 4-12 weeks after treatment initiation.

secondaryOutcomes.description: Time from treatment initiation to death from any cause.
Time from treatment initiation to radiologically confirmed disease progression (mRECIST) or death from any cause, whichever occurs first.
measured by psychologist using GAD-7 and PHQ-9, more than 10 points in either of the charts would be marked as positive

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Quality of Life Score (EORTC QLQ-C30, 0-100 scale)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Health-related quality of life will be assessed using the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core-30 (EORTC QLQ-C30). Scores for global health status/QoL, functional scales, and symptom scales will be calculated according to the EORTC scoring manual, with higher scores indicating better functioning for functional scales and worse symptoms for symptom scales.
